name: Rotational drive
description: Turns a motor's current into the angular acceleration of a link: the link's Angular velocity changes at Torque constant × current / Moment of inertia. Connect it from a Motor (it reads the Armature current) to a Rotational link (it changes the link's Angular velocity). Torque constant (N·m/A, default 0.1) is the torque the motor makes for each ampere. Moment of inertia (kg·m², default 0.01) is how much torque the link needs for each rad/s² of acceleration. It is simpler than Shaft dynamics, with no friction or load, and the link's angle is a state you can track and feed to a controller.
